name: momentum_reversal_regime_switch_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. This strategy uses ADX to detect the regime and switches between trend-following (ADX > 25) and mean-reversion (ADX < 18) approaches. In trending regimes: buy pullbacks to EMA(20). In range-bound regimes: fade VWAP extremes. The key insight is that the WRONG strategy in the wrong regime loses money — so regime detection is the alpha, not the individual entry rules. Edge persists because most traders pick one style and stick with it regardless of regime.

conditions: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close > ema_20 AND low touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 > 40 AND close > vwap
long.confirmation: trending: bounce off EMA20; range: vwap_zscore turning up

conditions: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close < ema_20 AND high touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 < 60 AND close < vwap
short.confirmation: trending: rejection at EMA20; range: vwap_zscore turning down

exit.trailing_stop: trending: trail by 1.0 * atr_20 after target; range: move SL to BE after +0.2%
exit.signal_exit: trending: close below ema_20; range: vwap_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: ADX is the regime filter itself
other_filters: ADX between 18-25 is a dead zone — no trades

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — regime-aware trading is more robust than single-style

weaknesses: ADX dead zone (18-25) means no trading during transitions — but transitions are where regime is most unclear
ADX on 1-min is slow to react — regime may have shifted before ADX reflects it
Two separate strategy logics increase complexity and parameter count (overfitting risk)
prior_art: Regime-switching models — Hamilton (1989). Practical implementation with ADX as regime proxy.
notes: Consider using a HMM (Hidden Markov Model) or ML classifier for more sophisticated regime detection.
